title: Isaiah Chapter 38 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 38 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 38 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 38.

questions.question: In Isaiah 38, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Isaiah the prophet came to Hezekiah
questions.explanation: This is stated as the first event in Isaiah 38:1, where it begins with Hezekiah's illness.

questions.question: Who came to Hezekiah when he was sick?
questions.explanation: Isaiah the prophet is mentioned in Isaiah 38:1 as the one who came to Hezekiah.

questions.question: What did Isaiah tell Hezekiah to do?
questions.explanation: Isaiah instructed Hezekiah to set his house in order in Isaiah 38:1.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do after Isaiah's message?
options: He set his house in order
questions.explanation: Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall and prayed unto the LORD as stated in Isaiah 38:2.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah remind the LORD of in his prayer?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah beseeched the LORD about how he walked before Him with a perfect heart in Isaiah 38:3.

questions.question: What was the LORD's response to Hezekiah's prayer?
options: He would add fifteen years to his life
He would send the king of Assyria away
questions.correctAnswer: He would add fifteen years to his life
questions.explanation: The LORD promised to add fifteen years to Hezekiah's life as stated in Isaiah 38:5.

questions.question: What did the LORD promise to deliver Hezekiah from?
questions.explanation: The LORD promised to deliver Hezekiah and the city from the king of Assyria in Isaiah 38:6.

questions.question: What sign did the LORD give to Hezekiah?
options: The shadow of the degrees would return
questions.correctAnswer: The shadow of the degrees would return
questions.explanation: The sign given was that the shadow of the degrees would return as stated in Isaiah 38:7.

questions.question: How many degrees would the shadow go backward?
questions.explanation: The shadow was to go back ten degrees as stated in Isaiah 38:8.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do after receiving the message from Isaiah?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah wept sore after Isaiah delivered the message from the LORD as stated in Isaiah 38:3.

questions.question: What was the relationship of the LORD to David mentioned in the message to Hezekiah?
questions.explanation: The LORD is referred to as the God of David thy father in Isaiah 38:5.

questions.question: True or False: Hezekiah prayed unto the LORD after hearing he would die.
questions.explanation: This is true as it is stated in Isaiah 38:2 that Hezekiah prayed after receiving the news.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD promised to add twenty years to Hezekiah's life.
questions.explanation: This is true as Isaiah 38:5 states that the LORD would add fifteen years to Hezekiah's life.

questions.question: True or False: Hezekiah was healed instantly after his prayer.
questions.explanation: This is false as the text does not state that he was healed instantly; it says he was given additional years.

questions.question: True or False: The king of Assyria was promised to attack Hezekiah's city.
questions.explanation: This is false; rather, the LORD promised to deliver Hezekiah from the hand of the king of Assyria in Isaiah 38:6.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 38 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 38 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah write after his recovery from sickness?
options: The writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick, and was recovered of his sickness
A prayer to the LORD for healing
A lament about his impending death
A song of praise to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick, and was recovered of his sickness
questions.explanation: This is correct as it is stated in Isaiah 38:9, which introduces the writing of Hezekiah after his recovery.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 38:16 promise will happen if someone lives by the things the Lord has spoken?
options: They will be blessed with wealth
They will be free from all troubles
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:16 states that by these things men live, indicating that God's promises lead to recovery and life.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah express about his life in Isaiah 38:12?
options: He felt his life was like a shepherd's tent
He was confident in his future
He was joyful about his recovery
He feared death would be a relief
questions.correctAnswer: He felt his life was like a shepherd's tent
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 38:12, Hezekiah compares his life to a shepherd's tent, indicating its temporary and fragile nature.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 38:14 reveal about Hezekiah's emotional state?
options: He was indifferent to his situation
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:14 describes Hezekiah mourning like a dove, indicating his sorrow and oppression.

questions.question: In Isaiah 38:10, what does Hezekiah say about his days?
options: He shall go to the gates of the grave
He will live to see many generations
He is grateful for his blessings
questions.correctAnswer: He shall go to the gates of the grave
questions.explanation: Hezekiah states in Isaiah 38:10 that he feels he will go to the gates of the grave, signifying his belief that he is nearing death.

questions.question: What does Hezekiah acknowledge about the LORD in Isaiah 38:15?
options: He has not heard my prayers
He hath both spoken unto me, and himself hath done it
He will not listen to my pleas
questions.correctAnswer: He hath both spoken unto me, and himself hath done it
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 38:15, Hezekiah recognizes that the LORD has both communicated with him and fulfilled His promise.

questions.question: How did Hezekiah respond to the message from the LORD in Isaiah 38:2?
options: He turned his face toward the wall and prayed
questions.correctAnswer: He turned his face toward the wall and prayed
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:2 states that Hezekiah turned to the wall and prayed, showing his immediate response to God's message.

questions.question: What did the LORD promise Hezekiah in Isaiah 38:5?
options: He would add fifteen years to his life
He would be made king again
He would be protected from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: He would add fifteen years to his life
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 38:5, the LORD explicitly states that He will add fifteen years to Hezekiah's life in response to his prayer.

questions.question: What metaphor does Hezekiah use to describe his suffering in Isaiah 38:13?
options: Like a bird in a cage
Like a lion breaking his bones
Like a tree in a storm
Like a ship lost at sea
questions.correctAnswer: Like a lion breaking his bones
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 38:13, Hezekiah compares his suffering to that of a lion breaking his bones, indicating the severity of his pain.

questions.question: What does Hezekiah ask the LORD to do in Isaiah 38:14?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah pleads with the LORD to undertake for him in Isaiah 38:14, expressing his need for divine intervention.

questions.question: In Isaiah 38:6, what additional promise does the LORD make to Hezekiah?
options: He will grant him eternal life
He will deliver him and the city from Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: He will deliver him and the city from Assyria
questions.explanation: The promise in Isaiah 38:6 includes the LORD's assurance to deliver Hezekiah and the city from the Assyrian threat.

questions.question: Hezekiah's prayer in Isaiah 38:3 demonstrates what aspect of his character?
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 38:3, Hezekiah's earnest prayer and plea for remembrance show his desperation for God's mercy amidst his crisis.

questions.question: Is it true that Hezekiah believed he would not see the LORD in the land of the living?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah expresses in Isaiah 38:11 that he believed he would not see the LORD in the land of the living, indicating his despair.

questions.question: Is it true that Hezekiah did not seek the LORD when he was sick?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:2 shows that Hezekiah turned to the LORD in prayer during his sickness, demonstrating his faith.

questions.question: Is it true that the LORD promised Hezekiah he would die immediately?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:5 indicates the LORD promised Hezekiah an extension of life, not immediate death.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 38 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 38.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 38:17, what did God do to Hezekiah's sins?
options: Cast all my sins behind thy back
Forgave only some of my sins
questions.correctAnswer: Cast all my sins behind thy back
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:17 states explicitly, 'for thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back,' indicating complete removal of sins by God.

questions.question: In Isaiah 38:18, what is said about the grave and death in relation to praising God?
options: The grave cannot praise thee, death cannot celebrate thee
The grave and death praise God loudly
The grave praises God with songs
questions.correctAnswer: The grave cannot praise thee, death cannot celebrate thee
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:18 clearly states, 'For the grave cannot praise thee, death cannot celebrate thee,' emphasizing that those who have died cannot praise God.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 38:19 say about who will praise God?
options: The living, the living, he shall praise thee
Only the elders shall praise thee
questions.correctAnswer: The living, the living, he shall praise thee
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:19 affirms, 'The living, the living, he shall praise thee,' indicating that praise comes from the living, not the dead.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 38:20, why will songs be sung in the house of the LORD?
options: Because the LORD was ready to save me
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD was ready to save me
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:20 states, 'The LORD was ready to save me: therefore we will sing my songs to the stringed instruments all the days of our life in the house of the LORD,' linking the singing directly to God's readiness to save.

questions.question: In Isaiah 38:21, what remedy did Isaiah instruct to be applied to Hezekiah's boil?
options: A lump of figs as a plaster
questions.correctAnswer: A lump of figs as a plaster
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:21 says, 'Let them take a lump of figs, and lay it for a plaister upon the boil, and he shall recover,' specifying the remedy clearly.

questions.question: What question did Hezekiah ask in Isaiah 38:22?
options: What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of the LORD?
Will the king of Assyria attack?
questions.correctAnswer: What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:22 records Hezekiah's question, 'What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of the LORD?'.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'chesed' (חֶסֶד) in Isaiah 38:17 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'chesed' in Isaiah 38:17 is translated as 'love' and denotes loyal lovingkindness or covenantal love, which is central to God's character.

questions.question: Which literary device is most prominently used in Isaiah 38:17-19, where contrasts between life and death and hope and despair are drawn?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:17-19 uses parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device, juxtaposing concepts such as bitterness and peace, the grave and the living to emphasize the contrast.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God casting sins away as in Isaiah 38:17?
questions.explanation: Micah 7:19 says, 'He will again have compassion on us; he will tread our iniquities underfoot,' echoing the theme of God removing sins similar to Isaiah 38:17.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with the sign given in Isaiah 38:8 about the shadow moving backward?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:9-11 recounts the same miracle of the shadow moving backward on the sundial of Ahaz, confirming the sign in Isaiah 38:8.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Isaiah's statement about the healing remedy in Isaiah 38:21?
options: The sign of the shadow moving backward
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:21 follows the narrative of Hezekiah's sickness and recovery, providing a detail of the physical remedy after the divine intervention.

questions.question: Which literary device is illustrated by the repetition in the phrase 'the living, the living' in Isaiah 38:19?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'the living, the living' in Isaiah 38:19 uses repetition to emphasize the importance of the living in praising God, a poetic device common in Hebrew literature.

questions.question: In the context of Isaiah 38, what typology does Hezekiah's healing foreshadow in the New Testament?
options: Christ's resurrection and victory over death
The coming of the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's resurrection and victory over death
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's healing and added years in Isaiah 38 typologically foreshadow Christ's resurrection and ultimate triumph over death, as death is shown powerless in verses 18-19.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 38:18 teaches that those who are dead can still hope for God's truth.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:18 states, 'they that go down into the pit cannot hope for thy truth,' indicating that the dead cannot hope for God's truth.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 38:22 records Hezekiah asking for a sign confirming his healing.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:22 records Hezekiah's question, 'What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of the LORD?', asking for confirmation of his recovery.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 38 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 38 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 38:3 teach about the nature of human righteousness before God?
options: Perfect human righteousness can earn salvation
Walking before God in truth and perfect heart is recognized by God
Human righteousness is irrelevant to God's judgment
Prayer can substitute for righteous living
questions.correctAnswer: Walking before God in truth and perfect heart is recognized by God
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:3 shows Hezekiah appealing to his walk before God in truth and with a perfect heart, implying that God acknowledges sincere and faithful living as significant.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine providence is taught in Isaiah 38:5 regarding human life and God's control?
options: God arbitrarily decides life spans without relation to prayer
God hears prayers and can extend life according to His will
questions.correctAnswer: God hears prayers and can extend life according to His will
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:5 reveals that God heard Hezekiah’s prayer and extended his life by fifteen years, teaching that God sovereignly responds to prayer within His providential will.

questions.question: What doctrine about death and the afterlife is implied in Isaiah 38:18?
options: The dead can praise God from the grave
Death is a state where one cannot hope for God's truth
The pit of death is a place of eternal praise
After death, souls immediately enter heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Death is a state where one cannot hope for God's truth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:18 states that the grave cannot praise God and death cannot celebrate Him, indicating that those in death cannot actively participate in worship or hope for God's truth.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 38:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:6 shows God promising to deliver Hezekiah and Jerusalem from the Assyrian king, demonstrating His faithfulness to the covenant promises made to David and his descendants.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Isaiah 38:8 through the sign given to Hezekiah?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:8 records the miraculous reversal of the sun's shadow, demonstrating God's sovereign power over natural creation.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 38:10-14 connect with the broader biblical theme of human mortality and reliance on God?
options: It prepares for the resurrection hope by depicting death's finality
It emphasizes human self-sufficiency in facing death
It denies the reality of death in the afterlife
It anticipates the establishment of earthly kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: It prepares for the resurrection hope by depicting death's finality
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:10-14 vividly describes the despair and finality of death, setting the stage for the biblical hope in resurrection and divine deliverance from death.

questions.question: In what way does the prayer and response in Isaiah 38:2-5 anticipate New Testament themes of intercession and divine mercy?
options: It shows that intercession is ineffective without sacrifice
It reveals God’s willingness to extend mercy in response to heartfelt prayer
It denies human participation in divine decisions
It asserts that prophets control God’s actions
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals God’s willingness to extend mercy in response to heartfelt prayer
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:2-5 illustrates that Hezekiah’s earnest prayer moved God to grant additional years, prefiguring the New Testament teaching on Christ’s intercession and God’s merciful response.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 38:17 and Isaiah 38:18 teach about sin, salvation, and human response?
options: Sin is ultimately forgiven by human effort alone
Salvation involves God’s loving forgiveness and the necessity of praising Him in life
The grave is a place of continued repentance and forgiveness
Death is the final opportunity to celebrate God’s truth
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation involves God’s loving forgiveness and the necessity of praising Him in life
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:17 speaks of God casting sins behind His back in love, while 38:18 highlights that the dead cannot praise God, teaching that salvation entails divine forgiveness and that praise must occur in the living.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine signs and assurance is taught in Isaiah 38:7-8 and Isaiah 38:21?
options: Divine signs are always natural phenomena without spiritual meaning
God uses both miracles and physical remedies as signs of His power and care
Physical healing is unrelated to divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: God uses both miracles and physical remedies as signs of His power and care
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:7-8 gives a miraculous sign of the sun’s shadow moving backward, and Isaiah 38:21 records the use of figs as a healing plaster, showing God’s provision through both miraculous and natural means.

questions.question: What combined theological theme is taught by Isaiah 38:9 and Isaiah 38:15 regarding the human experience of suffering and hope?
options: Suffering leads inevitably to despair without hope
Suffering is experienced deeply but is accompanied by a recognition of God's sovereignty and a hopeful spirit
Hope is irrelevant when facing death
Human lamentation is discouraged in Scripture
questions.correctAnswer: Suffering is experienced deeply but is accompanied by a recognition of God's sovereignty and a hopeful spirit
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:9 expresses the depth of Hezekiah’s suffering and impending death, while 38:15 acknowledges God’s involvement and the bittersweet hope to continue living, showing a complex interplay of lament and trust.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Isaiah 38:16-17 shows God arbitrarily deciding life without regard to human faith. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God’s decision to extend life is based solely on human merit
God’s loving deliverance comes in response to the life of the spirit and prayer
The passage denies any human role in salvation
questions.correctAnswer: God’s loving deliverance comes in response to the life of the spirit and prayer
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:16-17 emphasizes that men live by the life of the spirit and that God recovers and delivers according to His loving mercy, indicating a relational dynamic rather than arbitrary decision.

questions.question: What doctrine about human frailty and divine deliverance is taught in Isaiah 38:13?
options: Human life is secure apart from God
Human frailty is acute and God’s deliverance is necessary to prevent death
Death is a trivial event without spiritual significance
Suffering can be overcome by human willpower alone
questions.correctAnswer: Human frailty is acute and God’s deliverance is necessary to prevent death
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:13 describes the fear of death and the breaking of bones likened to a lion, underscoring human vulnerability and the need for divine intervention.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 38:20 specifically demonstrate in the context of divine salvation and worship?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:20 declares that the LORD was ready to save, linking divine salvation with worship and praise in the temple, highlighting God’s readiness and willingness to rescue His people.

questions.question: What theological theme is taught by Isaiah 38:14 regarding human lament and dependence on God?
options: Lament is a sign of weak faith
Lament expresses deep human distress and appeals for God’s intervention
God ignores human cries of distress
Humans should suppress mourning to maintain faith
questions.correctAnswer: Lament expresses deep human distress and appeals for God’s intervention
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:14 uses vivid imagery of chattering like a crane and mourning like a dove to express distress and a heartfelt plea for God’s help, showing lament as a legitimate spiritual expression.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 38:22 contribute to the narrative arc of divine-human communication through signs and worship?
options: It rejects the use of signs for confirming God’s promises
It shows the human desire for confirmation in approaching God’s presence
It teaches that worship is unnecessary
It denies the role of prophets in divine revelation
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the human desire for confirmation in approaching God’s presence
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:22 records Hezekiah asking for a sign that he may go up to the house of the LORD, illustrating the human need for assurance in coming before God, fitting the biblical theme of signs confirming divine promises.
